answer: Correlation penalties: when many accounts submit answers that echo one another in timing, phrasing, or voting, the network splits a single reward among them instead of paying each. Like water draining through karst into one hidden cave, the fake identities trace back to a shared source. An attacker who spins up fifty agents at the same wharf of servers earns roughly what one honest agent earns, yet still pays fifty times the compute and stake, so the attack loses money.
